notes.summary: Uniform pole contact and exact right-end geometry: moving contacts still give |R_sigma|<=1 and |sigma R_sigmasigma|<=5/4.
notes.detailedSummary: For every allowed obstacle, one left cutoff depends only on alpha,a,b,M. On x>b the gap is empty, one tangent segment ending at t, or one affine slope-one tail. The finite-contact slope defect is q B'(q), q=exp(-t). Explicit scalar formulas and weighted derivative bounds cover arbitrarily large t and changes between the right-end alternatives. These are analytic proofs using the imported full-envelope and convex-profile results.
notes.text:
Uniform radial lemmas for target I. Preserve D=i partial barpartial/(2pi), the standard normalized Fubini--Study kappa, genuine canonical potentials, and the FULL ordinary everywhere obstacle envelope. Write a0(x)=log(1+exp x), A=a0+psi, f_F=A+F, and C_F for the whole-line largest convex minorant. Imported supplied:n2 gives 0<A'<1, A''>0 and A''<=B_alpha=1/4+alpha(1-alpha), with the stated canonical ends. Imported supplied:n3 gives C_F in C^{1,1}, 0<=C_F'<=1 and 0<=C_F''<=sup max(f_F'',0) almost everywhere. Imported supplied:n4 identifies the envelope over all competitors with C_F-a0 and its genuine residual off the pole with R_F=C_F-A. The original competitor family is not restricted to radial functions.

Assume a<b; if a=b, a continuous function supported at that point is zero and I is immediate. The family condition implies ||F||_infinity<=M and ||F''||_infinity<=M. Therefore
|R_F|<=M, |R_F'|<=1, |R_F''|<=W:=2B_alpha+M almost everywhere. (1)
These are x derivatives. The first bound follows from A-||F||<=C_F<=A+F; the derivative bounds follow from the imported convex estimates. No third derivative bound is used.

Choose once t_-<min(a,0) such that
A(t_-)+A'(t_-)(b-t_-)<=A(a)-M. (2)
Such a choice exists: the left asymptotics give A(t)-tA'(t)=-(1-alpha)(1-t)^alpha+O(1), while bA'(t) tends to zero. For t<=t_-, the tangent ell_t(x)=A(t)+A'(t)(x-t) satisfies ell_t(b)<=ell_{t_-}(b), because differentiation in t gives A''(t)(b-t)>0 for t<b. On [a,b], ell_t(x)<=ell_t(b)<=A(a)-M<=A(x)+F(x). Outside [a,b], ell_t<=A=f_F by convexity. Thus ell_t is a whole-line admissible affine minorant. Since F(t)=0, C_F(t)=A(t) for every t<=t_-. Consequently every residual is exactly zero on one common neighborhood of the genuine pole. This cutoff depends only on alpha,a,b,M.

Classify the right region x>b, where f_F=A. Every strict-gap component is affine, and finite endpoints are contact points with matching derivatives. A finite gap with both endpoints >=b would be the chord of strictly convex A and hence strictly above A internally, a contradiction. An infinite gap with left endpoint >=b would have slope one by the end slope, contradicting derivative matching with A'<1. There cannot be two components meeting (b,infinity), since the later one would have left endpoint >=b. Therefore either C_F=A throughout (b,infinity), or the gap there is (b,t) for some finite t>b followed by C_F=A, or the gap is all of (b,infinity) and C_F=x+L. In the last case L=inf(f_F-x), with -M<=L<=0, by supplied:n3. In the finite case the affine segment is tangent to A at t. No assumption about the number of other free intervals is needed.

Set sigma=exp(-x) and
B(sigma)=log(1+sigma)+1-(1+log(1+sigma))^alpha,
so A(x)=x+B(exp(-x)). B is smooth on [0,infinity), B(0)=0 and B'(0)=1-alpha. With u=1+sigma and T=1+log u, direct differentiation gives
B'=(1-alpha T^{alpha-1})/u,
B''=(-1+alpha T^{alpha-1}+alpha(1-alpha)T^{alpha-2})/u^2.
The numerator of B'' lies between -1 and -(1-alpha)^2. Hence
0<B'<=1/u<=1, -1/u^2<=B''<0, sigma|B''|<=1/4. (3)
Also sigma B'(sigma)=1-A'(-log sigma) is strictly increasing: its derivative is A''(-log sigma)/sigma>0.

For a finite contact t let q=exp(-t) and d=1-A'(t)=qB'(q). The actual extended residual on 0<=sigma<exp(-b) is
R_F(sigma)=0 for 0<=sigma<=q,
R_F(sigma)=B(q)+d log(sigma/q)-B(sigma) for q<sigma<exp(-b). (4)
Values and first derivatives match at q. This follows directly from the tangent A(t)+A'(t)(x-t), with x-t=log(q/sigma). In the affine-tail case,
R_F(sigma)=L-B(sigma), including sigma=0. (5)
In the no-gap case it is zero.

On the free part of (4), monotonicity of sigma B' gives 0<=d/sigma<=B'(sigma). Thus
R_sigma=d/sigma-B'(sigma),
sigma R_sigmasigma=-d/sigma-sigma B''(sigma).
Together with (3), all alternatives satisfy
|R_sigma|<=1, |sigma R_sigmasigma|<=5/4 almost everywhere. (6)
The contact part is zero; (5) satisfies these bounds with d=0. Each scalar residual is C^1 through its finite cutoff. Its infinity value R_infinity is zero in (4) and L in (5), and integration gives
|R_F(sigma)-R_infinity|<=sigma. (7)
These weighted scalar estimates control projective derivatives without bounding the contact location or R_sigmasigma itself. They include the L=0 attained transition.

notes.summary: Target I's uniform global C^{1,1} bound proved in a fixed projective atlas, including explicit derivative bounds through both ends.
notes.detailedSummary: A fixed chart norm admits K=M+U+H with explicit constants depending only on the prescribed parameters. The infinity Hessian is bounded by 22 on the larger charts independently of contact locations. Normal gradients vanish uniformly at infinity, tangential gradients vanish quadratically, and the residual is zero on a common pole neighborhood. Weak Hessian bounds give the global Lipschitz-gradient estimate.
notes.text:
Uniform global C^{1,1} proof. Use n1 with W=2B_alpha+M and its fixed t_-. Specify the atlas and norm. In projective chart Z_j!=0 let W_j be the coordinate polydisc where every ratio Z_i/Z_j, i!=j, has modulus <2. Let V_j have all these moduli <3/2. The V_j cover P^k, since choosing a largest homogeneous coordinate makes every ratio <=1. Their closures lie in W_j. Use real Euclidean gradient norms and Hessian operator norms, and define
||u||_{C^{1,1}}=||u||_infinity+max_j sup_{V_j}|Du_j|+max_j Lip_{V_j}(Du_j). (8)
Other fixed finite smooth projective atlas norms differ by fixed comparison constants. We establish bounds on the larger W_j.

On W_0 use z_i=Z_i/Z_0 and x=log|z|^2. Every residual is exactly zero for x<=t_-, including z=0. For x>t_-,
|Dx|=2/|z|<=2 exp(-t_-/2), ||D^2x||=2/|z|^2<=2 exp(-t_-).
The chain rule and n1(1) give
|DR_F|<=U_0:=2 exp(-t_-/2),
||D^2R_F||<=H_0:=(4W+2)exp(-t_-) almost everywhere. (9)
The zero extension crosses the genuine pole without subtracting two infinite values.

For j>=1 write tau=Z_0/Z_j, xi=(Z_i/Z_j)_{i!=0,j}, and S=1+|xi|^2. Away from tau=0,
x=log S-log|tau|^2, sigma=|tau|^2/S.
Where x<=b, |tau|^2>=S exp(-b), and real block differentiation gives
|Dx|^2=4/|tau|^2+4|xi|^2/S^2<=4exp(b)+1,
||D^2x||<=2 max(exp(b),1).
Consequently
|DR_F|<=U_c:=sqrt(4exp(b)+1),
||D^2R_F||<=H_c:=W(4exp(b)+1)+2 max(exp(b),1) almost everywhere. (10)
These estimates include arbitrary finite free boundaries, including accumulating components, through the uniform Lipschitz bound of C_F'. They do not assert continuous second derivatives at a free boundary.

Where x>b, use n1(6). On W_j, |tau|<2 and sigma<=4. Direct differentiation gives
|D sigma|^2=4sigma/S+4sigma^2|xi|^2/S^2<=4sigma+sigma^2<=8sigma,
||D^2 sigma||<=12. (11)
For the latter bound put g=1/S. Its real gradient has norm <=1 and its real Hessian has norm <=2: the tangential eigenvalue is -2/S^2 and the radial eigenvalue is (-2+6|xi|^2)/S^3, both bounded in absolute value by 2. The tau-tau block of D^2sigma has norm <=2, the xi-xi block <=2|tau|^2<=8, and the cross block <=2|tau|<=4. The diagonal matrix has norm <=8 and the off-diagonal matrix <=4, proving 12.

Thus
|DR_F|<=sqrt(8sigma)<=2sqrt(2)|tau|<=U_infinity:=4sqrt(2),
||D^2R_F||<=12+8(5/4)=H_infinity:=22 almost everywhere. (12)
These constants contain no contact location or inverse contact radius. More precisely,
|D_tau R_F|<=2|tau|/S<=2|tau|,
|D_xi R_F|<=2sigma|xi|/S<=sigma,
|R_F-R_infinity|<=sigma<=|tau|^2. (13)
All first derivatives therefore extend continuously as zero on the infinity hyperplane.

Each individual residual is smooth near infinity. In the finite-contact or no-gap case it is zero there. In the affine-tail case it is L-B(|tau|^2/S). At tau=0 its real normal Hessian is exactly -2(1-alpha)S^{-1}I_2, and its tangential and mixed Hessian blocks are zero. In the other alternative every block is zero. Both obey (12). At the pole every derivative is zero on the common neighborhood.

Set
U=max(U_0,U_c,4sqrt(2)),
H=max(H_0,H_c,22),
K=M+U+H. (14)
The canonical formulas and profile regularity in n1 give a continuous, locally Lipschitz gradient. Equations (9)--(12) uniformly bound its weak Hessian almost everywhere on each convex W_j. A continuous locally Lipschitz field with weak derivative norm <=H on a convex domain is H-Lipschitz: mollify around a compact segment, integrate the derivative estimate along that segment, and pass to the continuous limit. This avoids exceptional-line issues with almost-everywhere Hessians. Therefore Lip_{W_j}DR_F<=H, and (8) yields ||R_F||_{C^{1,1}}<=K for every allowed F.

All constants are finite and depend only on alpha,a,b,M through n1's fixed choice of t_-. Dependence on k or another fixed atlas enters only through fixed norm comparisons. There is no uniform right cutoff assumption, no third derivative hypothesis, and no closed minimal-type uniqueness argument. This proves the first assertion of I globally.

notes.summary: Target I's C^{1,gamma} stability proved with exponent (1-gamma)/2 for every 0<gamma<1.
notes.detailedSummary: Constant-one C^0 stability combines with the uniform Hessian bound on larger charts. Taylor's formula gives a gradient bound proportional to sqrt(delta). Interpolation between gradient amplitude and Lipschitz bounds gives the stated Hölder exponent with an explicit K_gamma. Both end-alternative transitions and canonical extensions are included; C^{1,1} convergence is not inferred.
notes.text:
Global interpolation proof. Let u=R_F-R_G and delta=||F-G||_infinity<=1. Imported supplied:n4 gives ||u||_infinity<=delta for the actual canonically extended residuals, including their pole and infinity values. Its whole-line convex-minorant proof uses monotonicity and commutation with constants, and applies to every pair in this family. If delta=0, the residuals coincide.

Use the larger W_j and smaller V_j of n2, with H from n2(14). The chart gradient of u has Lipschitz constant <=2H on W_j. If p belongs to V_j, e is a real unit vector, and 0<h<=r_0:=1/4, the segment p+[0,h]e lies in W_j. Taylor's formula gives
|u(p+he)-u(p)-h Du(p).e|<=Hh^2.
Both function values have absolute value <=delta, hence
|Du(p).e|<=2delta/h+Hh.
Choose h=r_0 sqrt(delta) and maximize over e:
sup_{V_j}|Du|<=A_*sqrt(delta), A_*:=8+H/4. (15)
The chart margin makes this valid even near the boundaries of V_j.

For p,q in V_j, convexity and the Lipschitz-gradient bound yield
|Du(p)-Du(q)|<=min(2A_*sqrt(delta),2H|p-q|).
Since min(s,t)<=s^{1-gamma}t^gamma for positive s,t and 0<gamma<1,
[Du]_{C^{0,gamma}(V_j)}<=(2A_*)^{1-gamma}(2H)^gamma delta^{(1-gamma)/2}. (16)
Define the fixed-atlas C^{1,gamma} norm as sup|u| plus the maximum chart gradient sup and maximum chart gradient gamma seminorm. Because delta<=1, delta and sqrt(delta) are each <=delta^{(1-gamma)/2}. Thus
K_gamma=1+A_*+(2A_*)^{1-gamma}(2H)^gamma (17)
satisfies
||R_F-R_G||_{C^{1,gamma}}<=K_gamma delta^{(1-gamma)/2}.
A different fixed finite smooth projective atlas introduces only fixed norm-comparison constants. The parameter dependence is exactly the allowed dependence on k,alpha,a,b,M and gamma, with the atlas fixed.

The argument uses actual global C^0 and C^{1,1} bounds, so it includes crossing the genuine pole and infinity hyperplane and every change of right-end alternative. No contact cutoff appears. It proves the second assertion of I for every pair and every 0<gamma<1. Uniform Hessian boundedness does not imply small Hessian differences, so C^{1,1} convergence is not claimed.

notes.detailedSummary: A vertical quadratic gives canonical slice restrictions with the exact horizontal kappa bound. Thus all H-psh competitors lie below the pulled-back base envelope, without Y symmetry or closedness. The residual is the pullback of R_F, with zero vertical derivatives and controlled extension across the pole fiber and infinity divisor. notes.text:
Product extension of I. Fix any connected compact complex m-fold Y with smooth positive Hermitian form h0. Put X=P^k times Y and H=pi^*kappa+pr_Y^*h0. This is positive and big in the exact definition, with rho=0, epsilon=1 and h=H. Closedness is not assumed. Pull back the stated reference and each allowed F, and retain the full everywhere ordinary obstacle operator.

These hypotheses match supplied:n6. The canonical restriction argument also checks the indispensable all-competitor condition directly. For a genuine H-psh competitor v, choose a product coordinate box, a smooth local kappa-potential b(z), and vertical coordinates w. Choose c>0 with h0<=cD|w|^2 there. Then the genuine representative v+b(z)+c|w|^2 is psh, since
D[v+b+c|w|^2]>=cD|w|^2-h0>=0.
Canonical holomorphic restriction of psh functions, from supplied:n1, gives a psh restriction to w=w0 or the identically minus-infinity restriction. The vertical quadratic becomes constant, leaving exactly kappa+D_z v(.,w0)>=0. There is no horizontal error and no local potential for nonclosed h0 is needed. The local restrictions glue; connectedness propagates the genuine or identically minus-infinity alternative across P^k.

Every nontrivial slice satisfies v(.,w0)<=psi+F everywhere and v(.,w0) preceq psi with the inherited order constant. It is therefore a competitor for the full base envelope and lies below E_F pointwise, including canonical pole values. Identically minus-infinity slices do also. Thus every product competitor is <=pi^*E_F. Conversely pi^*E_F is genuine and admissible because
H+D pi^*E_F=pi^*(kappa+DE_F)+pr_Y^*h0>=0,
and it satisfies the obstacle and ordinary order. Hence E_F^H=pi^*E_F with the canonical global representatives, as in supplied:n6.

The retained residual is R_F^H=pi^*R_F, with its forced value zero on {0} times Y. Choose a fixed finite smooth atlas of Y with nested precompact domains and form product charts with n2's W_j,V_j. Vertical first and second derivatives vanish; horizontal derivatives are exactly those of R_F. The C^{1,1} estimate of n2 therefore holds in product chart norms. For n3's Hölder seminorm, product Euclidean distance is at least horizontal distance, so vertical changes cannot enlarge it. Both estimates hold with the same constants in these product norms. Any other fixed atlas or metric introduces only fixed geometry constants, as allowed in I.

There is a common neighborhood {x<=t_-} times Y where every residual and all its derivatives vanish. Across the infinity hyperplane times Y, the actual value is R_infinity, every first derivative vanishes, vertical derivatives vanish, and the horizontal derivative estimates and Hessian alternatives are exactly n2(12)--(13). This establishes actual crossing of both geometric sets for the full nonclosed operator.

In particular the conclusion applies to P^2 times the standard Hopf surface from supplied:n7, whose specified h0 is positive and nonclosed and whose product is non-Kahler. No lower-mass property, BMP, Y symmetry or closed-class uniqueness is used. Existing actual-mass results are unchanged. The exact stretching certificate can also be retained: handle t=1 separately with a=E_F^H, avoiding 0 times minus infinity. For t>1 choose a_t=psi-t||F||_infinity. Then t^{-1}a_t+(1-t^{-1})psi=psi-||F||_infinity<=E_F^H with genuine pole values. These are direct witnesses for the supplied E_env definition.

notes.summary: One controlled family provably has contact cutoffs tending to infinity and changes its right-end alternative; lightweight numerical diagnostics are consistent with the formulas.
notes.detailedSummary: The C^2 bump chi=(1-x^2)^3 on [-1,1] satisfies ||chi||+||chi''||=7. A critical lambda_c in (0,1) separates zero-unattained L, zero-attained L, and negative L. Finite right contacts tend to infinity below the critical value, while above it an actual affine zero-density tail occurs. Numerical estimates for alpha=0.6 illustrate this behavior but are uncertified observations.
notes.text:
A changing-end family inside fixed parameters. Fix any 0<alpha<1 and k>=2, take [a,b]=[-1,1] and M=7, and define chi(x)=(1-x^2)^3 for |x|<1 and zero otherwise. Let F_lambda=-lambda chi, 0<=lambda<=1. The boundary values of chi, chi' and chi'' vanish, so chi is C^2 with the required support. Internally chi''=-6+36x^2-30x^4, whose minimum is -6 and maximum 24/5. Therefore ||chi||=1, ||chi''||=6 and ||F_lambda||+||F_lambda''||=7lambda<=7.

Using B from n1, define the exact number lambda_c=min_{-1<x<1} B(exp(-x))/chi(x). The positive ratio tends to infinity at both endpoints, so its minimum is attained at an interior y and is positive. At x=0 the ratio is B(1)<log 2<1, hence 0<lambda_c<1. For lambda<lambda_c, f_lambda-x is strictly positive everywhere and tends to zero at plus infinity: L=0 is unattained. At lambda=lambda_c it is nonnegative and vanishes at y: L=0 is attained. For lambda>lambda_c it is negative at y: L<0 is attained. Thus all right-end alternatives occur in this one controlled family. Supplied:n3 gives C_c(x)=x for x>=y and an affine right tail above the critical value. Supplied:n5 identifies an open part of that latter tail as an actual zero-density region. The uniform residual estimates apply there and through its finite free boundaries.

The finite right cutoff tends to infinity as lambda increases to lambda_c from below. Supplied:n4 gives ||C_lambda-C_c||_infinity<=lambda_c-lambda. For any fixed T>1, A(T)-T=B(exp(-T))>0. If 0<lambda_c-lambda<B(exp(-T)), then C_lambda(T)<=T+(lambda_c-lambda)<A(T). Thus T belongs to the right gap. The zero-unattained alternative supplies a finite right cutoff t_lambda, and n1's classification gives t_lambda>T. Since T is arbitrary, t_lambda tends to infinity. This analytic example verifies that the difficult family quantifier is nonvacuous.
